prompt:
Find what the Debian project officially states about the support period of a stable release, including LTS. Cite the Debian page and quote the relevant statement.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Debian project officially states that a standard stable release receives support for approximately 3 years. After this period, support is extended by the Debian Long Term Support (LTS) team for an additional 2 years, bringing the total support period to roughly 5 years. 

Below are the cited sources for both the standard stable support period and the LTS support period:

SOURCE: https://www.debian.org/releases/ | QUOTE: "Debian provides more than a pure OS: it comes with over 59000 packages, precompiled software bundled up in a nice format for easy installation on your machine. A stable release is supported for approximately 3 years." | CLAIM: The official support period for a standard Debian stable release is approximately 3 years.

SOURCE: https://wiki.debian.org/LTS | QUOTE: "Debian Long Term Support (LTS) is a project to extend the lifetime of all Debian stable releases to (at least) 5 years." | CLAIM: The Debian LTS project extends the total support period of a stable release to at least 5 years, adding approximately 2 years of support after the standard 3-year period ends.
